questions.explanation: Metabolism covers all pathways; catabolism breaks molecules down; anabolism builds larger molecules.

prompt.text: Complete the sentence about energy in catabolic and anabolic pathways.

questions.explanation: Catabolism releases free energy (exergonic); anabolism requires free energy input (endergonic).

questions.explanation: In thermodynamics, energetically favorable processes are called spontaneous (ΔG < 0).

prompt.text: A spontaneous reaction will have a Gibbs free energy that:

questions.explanation: Spontaneous reactions have negative Gibbs free energy (ΔG < 0).

prompt.text: A spontaneous reaction that occurs will be:

questions.explanation: Exergonic reactions release free energy and are spontaneous as written.

prompt.text: Order these molecules from least to most efficient for extracting ATP.

questions.explanation: Per gram, fats yield the most ATP; glucose is intermediate; amino acids are generally least efficient as fuel in this ranking.

prompt.text: The energy barrier that molecules must overcome for a reaction to proceed is known as:

questions.explanation: Activation energy is the energy barrier that must be cleared for reactants to form products.

prompt.text: A substrate binds to an enzyme at its:

questions.explanation: Substrates bind the enzyme’s active site where catalysis occurs.

prompt.text: True or false: Cooperative enzymes do not require separate activators or inhibitors.

questions.explanation: Cooperativity can arise from substrate binding alone; dedicated activators or inhibitors are not always required.

prompt.text: The first substrate to bind to a cooperative enzyme has _____ affinity.

questions.explanation: In cooperative enzymes, the first substrate binds with lower affinity; subsequent binding becomes easier.

questions.explanation: Feedback inhibition typically has the end product bind an allosteric site on an earlier enzyme.
